summary: Two source banks cannot be replayed, and hard generation excludes a supported operation family. Tested mathematics, grading, rendering and packaging pass. Package files remain unchanged.

source_analysis.skill: Apply specified elementary row operations to a coefficient matrix and select the resulting matrix.
reasoning_steps: Identify the operation and indexed row roles.
Apply it to every entry of each destination row, preserving unassigned rows.
For two operations, use the intermediate matrix.
invariants: Nonzero scaling and distinct donor/destination rows.
One operation for easy/moderate; two additions for hard.
permitted_variations: Matrix entries, eligible row roles, factors and choice positions.
Hard operations sharing either a destination or a donor.
Optional cancellation without fixing which entry becomes zero.

source_replay.details: Nine complete source banks reproduce; q-10251 and q-10243 raise unknown-profile errors.

math.details: 199 independently parsed records have correct keys, unique choices and correct final solution matrices. Additional target cases also agree.

variety.details: Hard production structurally excludes distinct destinations. Easy controls cover swaps and scaling; the exact five-item batch contains swaps only.

scope.details: Tested instances preserve the source operations, representations, response format and workload.

grading.details: Native grader: 21 correct-choice acceptances and 84 wrong-choice rejections; zero unresolved.

rendering.details: Actual UI reports pass; inspected screenshots show readable matrices, controls and worked steps.

packaging.details: Exact Python dependency version matches. Deterministic replay, relocation and rejection checks pass. Recursive package hashes are unchanged.

decision_variation.details: Controlled easy changes pass, and no universal tested shortcut answers the exact batch. Hard destination relationships remain unjustifiably fixed. Delivery retained all tested easy records; live policy/history limitations are documented.

findings.description: Hard production always updates one destination twice, excluding three supplied shared-donor/two-destination cases.
findings.reproduction: Run regressions.py. Source q-130064 requires R1:=R1-2R2 followed by R3:=R3+R2. Normal hard seeds 72011–72070 all repeat one destination. hard.operations() explicitly emits p['target'] twice, proving structural exclusion.
